finding.claim: Each JWT with an unseen kid triggers a synchronous, uncapped outbound fetch to {authority}/token_keys, enabling unauthenticated IdP amplification and request-thread blocking.
finding.source: kid header of any JWT sent to an endpoint protected by the JwtBearer scheme (no prior auth needed)
finding.sink: TokenKeyResolver.FetchKeySetAsync -> httpClient.SendAsync, blocked via GetAwaiter().GetResult() with CancellationToken.None (line 111)

trace.note: IssuerSigningKeyResolver passes header keyId straight to ResolveSigningKey
cache miss for a new kid triggers FetchKeySet
blocking fetch with no cancellation token
negative cache for 30-60s applies only to the same kid

finding.guards_checked: Signatures are still verified; the authority comes from config (no SSRF); negative caching only limits repeats of the same kid; no rate limit, concurrency cap, or MemoryCache size limit exists. Impact is availability/amplification, not auth bypass. OIDC copy (Authentication.OpenIdConnect/TokenKeyResolver.cs, PostConfigureOpenIdConnectOptions.cs:70-72) has the same structure.

finding.claim: Environment endpoint redaction matches key names only by suffix, so secret values whose key contains a keyword but does not end with it are returned unmasked.
finding.source: config/environment variable name and value; the caller must be able to read the env actuator (default RequiredPermissions=Full, i.e. read_sensitive_data under CF; app-secured management endpoints elsewhere)
finding.sink: EnvironmentEndpointHandler sanitized value returned in the env actuator response (EnvironmentEndpointHandler.cs:84-85)

trace.note: default sanitized keys: password, secret, key, token, .*credentials.*, vcap_services, .*connectionstring.*
a name like SECRET_KEY_BASE ends in BASE, so no pattern matches
only password=/pwd= pairs and URI user-info are masked for non-matching keys (lines 55-56)

finding.guards_checked: Full-permission gate on the env endpoint; VCAP_SERVICES and credentials defaults; password=/pwd= and URI user-info masking. These do not cover secret-bearing names where the keyword is not a suffix.

finding.claim: On the management port, non-actuator (application) paths are allowed when the request scheme does not match, so app routes are reachable through the management port. Low confidence: a design-contract issue, not a demonstrated actuator-protection bypass.
finding.source: request reaching the management port; Request.Scheme may be altered by forwarded-headers middleware (X-Forwarded-Proto) if the app enables it

trace.note: port uses real Connection.LocalPort (not spoofable), plus CF_INSTANCE_PORTS mapping
non-actuator path allowed on scheme mismatch

finding.guards_checked: Actuator paths still require both scheme and real LocalPort; app-level auth and the CF security middleware remain in the pipeline; no actuator data reachable via this path.
